```{r}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(rpart)        # for building trees
library(rpart.plot)   # for plotting trees
library(randomForest) # for bagging & forests
library(infer)        # for resampling
kangaroos <- read.csv("https://ajohns24.github.io/data/kangaroo.csv")
head(kangaroos)
kangaroos <- kangaroos |>
  mutate(species = as.factor(species))
```

# 2. Technical details


```{r}
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8

# STEP 1: tree specification with specific tuning parameter values
tree_spec <- decision_tree() |>
  set_mode("classification") |> 
  set_engine(engine = "rpart") |> 
  set_args(cost_complexity = 0, min_n = 2, tree_depth = 30)

# STEP 2: Build the tree!
# Note that we specified our tuning parameters in Step 1.
# Thus no tuning (hence no workflows) necessary.
kangaroo_tree <- tree_spec |> 
  fit(species ~ ., data = kangaroos)

# Plot the tree
kangaroo_tree |> 
  extract_fit_engine() |> 
  plot(margin = 0) 
kangaroo_tree |> 
  extract_fit_engine() |> 
  text(cex = 0.7)
```


```{r}
#| eval: false
# There's randomness behind the splits!

set.seed(253)
    
# STEP 1: Model Specification
rf_spec <- rand_forest()  |>
  set_mode("classification") |>
  set_engine(engine = "ranger") |> 
  set_args(
    mtry = NULL,
    trees = 500,
    min_n = 2,
    probability = FALSE,    # Report classifications, not probability calculations
    importance = "impurity" # Use Gini index to measure variable importance
  )
    
# STEP 2: Build the forest
# There are no preprocessing steps or tuning, hence no need for a workflow!
kangaroo_forest <- rf_spec |> 
  fit(species ~ ., data = kangaroos)
```



```{r}
kangaroo_forest
```

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 10
# Print the metrics
kangaroo_forest |>
  extract_fit_engine() |>
  pluck("variable.importance") |> 
  sort(decreasing = TRUE)
    
# Plot the metrics
library(vip)
kangaroo_forest |> 
  vip(geom = "point", num_features = 20)
```
```{r}
#| eval: true
# The cbind() includes the original candy data
# alongside their predicted popularity levels
kangaroo_forest |> 
  predict(new_data = kangaroos) |> 
  cbind(kangaroos) |> 
  conf_mat(
    truth = species,
    estimate = .pred_class
  )
```
```{r}
#Overall accuracy
(49+42+35)/148
```
Better at predicting fulginosus species compared to others
